thread: Ava: Heads-up — follow-up from the tombstone RFC: we need a concrete plan for how tombstones propagate through router -> runtime -> client SDKs. Short thread to align.
messages:
Ava: Heads-up — follow-up from the tombstone RFC: we need a concrete plan for how tombstones propagate through router -> runtime -> client SDKs. Short thread to align.
Sam: +1. Current concern: if we mark a field as tombstoned in the catalog, how do downstream rpcs stop reading it without breaking older clients?
Priya: My rough take: two-step deprecate: 1) soft-tombstone (silent ignore at runtime but still emitted in responses), 2) hard-tombstone (removed from responses). Soft period gives us telemetry.
Liam: Important: router must advertise capability via header so runtime can decide whether to include the field. Otherwise clients will see inconsistent responses.
Ava: Agreed. Proposal: add a negotiation header X-RW-Compat that lists opt-in features, e.g., {"tombstone-v1":"aware"}. If header absent, runtime defaults to include field for safety.
Sam: That helps. But we also need a shim for SDKs that assume the field exists. How long do we run the shim?
Priya: TTL-based rollout. Soft-tombstone window = 30d by default. During that window: runtime emits a warning metric when client requests without the opt-in header. SDKs ship a compatibility layer that maps missing field -> fallback value and logs a deprecation notice to telemetry.
Liam: Operationally: set tenant-level policy with three flags: soft_tombstone_ts, hard_tombstone_ts, and enforce_opt_in. The router consults policy and rewrites header to indicate opt-in if tenant has opted in.
Ava: For multi-tenant Dedicated customers, we should allow per-tenant override. Also add a safety circuit: if error rates spike after hard tombstone, auto-roll back to include field and page on-call.
Sam: How do we collect signal? Suggest two telemetry streams: 1) presence/absence metric per route, 2) client-side warnings from SDKs with debug sampling (~0.1%). Correlate with errors/latency anomalies.
Priya: Also need migration helper: a small admin API endpoint that can produce a report listing active tenants and SDK versions observed that request the old field. This lets PMs phase customers.
Liam: Implementation notes: router changes are lightweight — add header enrichment and policy lookup cache. Runtime needs a fast path: if opt-in header set, skip legacy emission; else include field. Keep branch cheap to avoid perf regressions.
Ava: Security/compat: treat tombstone metadata as non-sensitive but sign it in internal RPCs so sidecars can't be spoofed. DevBot: deploy plan created — staging tomorrow at 03:00 UTC, canary 10% for 24h, then ramp.
Sam: One more: document the SDK shim API. Example (JS):
```js
// before
const val = resp.oldField || defaultVal
// after (shim)
const val = resp.oldField ?? shim.getFallback('oldField')
```
Priya: + add a README snippet recommending opt-in header usage for early adopters.
Ava: OK. Action items: Priya draft SDK shim spec + README (due EOD). Liam add router policy flags + caching (PR by Thursday). Sam add telemetry dashboards and alert rules (PR by Friday). I'll draft rollback runbook.
Priya: I'll also add the admin report endpoint proposal to the RFC doc.
Liam: Noted. If we hit unexpected regressions, revert router header enrichment first — low blast radius.
Ava: Thanks all. If no objections I'll post a short RFC update summarizing these decisions. :thumbsup:
Sam: LGTM
Priya: LGTM
DevBot: Staging deploy scheduled at 2026-03-25T03:00:00Z (pipeline #4521).
